filter_note: V1 set (7) + market briefing + AI news; Today window = Wed Oct 28 – Thu Oct 29 PT

market_briefing.lede: AI tools are moving from per-seat licenses to shared, metered budgets: GitHub now includes Copilot with every GitHub Enterprise seat and meters usage against one enterprise budget, and Claude Enterprise lets admins give each team a single pooled monthly budget. Governed workflow actions also keep moving into assistants, with ServiceNow's plugin now live in ChatGPT.

bullets.text: Claude Enterprise smart reports, in-app surveys and pooled group budgets became generally available on Oct 28. Reports group a team's sessions into workstreams with spend and friction per workstream and recommend recurring workflows to turn into skills; budget alerts go to billing admins at 50%, 75%, 95% and 100%.

From Oct 28, eligible GitHub Enterprise Cloud customers can get Copilot for every licensed user, with AI usage metered against the enterprise budget. Shared Copilot Automations, team-owned workflows with prompts, triggers and allowed tools, are rolling out and bill to the repository owner.

OpenAI and ServiceNow expanded their partnership on Oct 28. A ServiceNow MCP plugin is in the OpenAI marketplace now, letting users update ServiceNow records from ChatGPT while ServiceNow's Action Fabric applies each customer's existing rules and permissions.

biggest_ai_news.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon
biggest_ai_news.body: Oct 28: Google's new frontier model leads on cybersecurity and long-running coding benchmarks. It goes first to a subset of cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program, with wider developer and business access later, at an introductory $2/$10 per million input/output tokens (then $4/$20).

biggest_ai_news.title: Microsoft opens its Copilot harness to enterprise developers
biggest_ai_news.body: Oct 28: the multi-model harness behind GitHub Copilot and Copilot Studio is in public preview in Microsoft Foundry, handling tools, sandboxing, policy and model routing across 20+ OpenAI and Anthropic models. Free through Nov 30, then billed on compute and memory, with no per-seat charge.

biggest_ai_news.title: ChatGPT Business and Pro subscriptions now carry API credits
biggest_ai_news.body: Eligible subscribers can link a paid ChatGPT plan to an API organization they own and claim monthly API credits: $20 per Standard seat and $100 per Premium seat, capped at $500 per Business workspace, expiring each billing cycle.

biggest_ai_news.title: Nadella pitches Microsoft Execution Containers as the agent control layer
biggest_ai_news.body: On Microsoft's Oct 28 earnings call, Satya Nadella called MXC a policy-driven layer that "governs and contains agents" across Windows and other platforms and said OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta's Muse are adopting it.

what_changed.title: OpenAI and ServiceNow put governed ServiceNow actions inside ChatGPT
what_changed.body: NEW (adjacent). Oct 28: a ServiceNow MCP plugin is available in the OpenAI marketplace, with enhanced capabilities by end of 2026. Customers choose which capabilities to expose, and ServiceNow's Action Fabric enforces existing rules and permissions. Codex in AI Workflow Factory is planned for 2027, and all ServiceNow employees will get ChatGPT Work and Codex.

what_changed.title: Claude Enterprise adds pooled team budgets and usage reports
what_changed.body: NEW (adjacent). Oct 28: smart reports, in-app surveys and pooled group budgets are GA. A group shares one monthly budget while per-member limits still apply; members can request more from inside Claude, and setup suggests an amount from recent usage.

what_changed.title: GitHub bundles Copilot into GitHub Enterprise and adds shared Automations
what_changed.body: NEW (adjacent). Oct 28 at GitHub Universe: eligible Enterprise Cloud customers can include Copilot for every licensed user, with usage against the enterprise budget; self-serve availability is staged. Shared Copilot Automations let anyone with write access edit team workflows, which run in the cloud and bill to the repository owner.

what_changed.title: Salesforce publishes Pronto, an open-source sample app for its Headless Toolkit
what_changed.body: NEW. Oct 28: Pronto shows two Agentforce agents with 16+ actions, hosted MCP servers and multi-agent orchestration, with Salesforce data and workflows surfaced in Claude, Slack and Agentforce Coworker.

quiet_note: No new Gong, Clay, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft or Monaco launches found for Oct 28–29. Oct 28 press about Salesloft Agentic Playbook recaps the Oct 27 announcement already covered.

market_direction.label: Falling (per-seat licensing as the main AI meter)
market_direction.text: GitHub Enterprise includes Copilot for every licensed user and meters usage against one budget (Oct 28); Microsoft's Copilot harness has no per-seat charge (Oct 28).

market_direction.label: Accelerating (team-level AI spend controls)
market_direction.text: Claude Enterprise pooled group budgets and smart reports GA (Oct 28); Copilot Automations add cost controls and bill to the repository owner (Oct 28).

market_direction.label: Accelerating (governed business actions inside ChatGPT)
market_direction.text: ServiceNow MCP plugin in the OpenAI marketplace with Action Fabric permissions (Oct 28), a day after Oracle AI Workspace for ChatGPT (Oct 27).

market_direction.label: Emerging (managed multi-model agent harnesses)
market_direction.text: Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry public preview with built-in model routing (Oct 28).

language_pulse.gloss: Anthropic's term for one shared monthly AI budget per team, with individual limits kept as guardrails (Oct 28).
Microsoft's word for the layer above the model that manages context, tools, sandboxing, policy and model routing (Oct 28).
ServiceNow's name for its layer that orchestrates and governs AI across the enterprise, used in the OpenAI announcement (Oct 28).

competitive_moves.text: Pronto open-source sample app for the Headless Toolkit (Oct 28); Agentforce Coworker explainer for startups and SMBs stressing confirm-before-save record edits (Oct 28).

watch.title: Salesloft Behind Every Win summit (Nov 4) and Salesforce Agent Evals beta (November)
watch.body: Watch whether Salesloft gives Agentic Playbook pricing or a GA date on Nov 4, and whether Salesforce or the revenue vendors answer ServiceNow's ChatGPT plugin with their own governed actions inside ChatGPT, or move to pooled, metered AI budgets the way GitHub and Anthropic just did.

interpretation.fact: On Oct 28, OpenAI and ServiceNow expanded their partnership and put a ServiceNow MCP plugin in the OpenAI marketplace; Claude Enterprise made smart reports, surveys and pooled group budgets GA; GitHub began including Copilot with GitHub Enterprise and rolled out shared Copilot Automations; Microsoft opened its Copilot harness in Foundry; Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon; and Salesforce published the Pronto sample app. OpenAI's help center describes API credits of up to $500 per ChatGPT Business workspace.
interpretation.note: Light interpretation: none of the watchlist vendors shipped anything new on Oct 28–29. The adjacent signal is about how AI gets bought and controlled: budgets are moving from seats to shared, metered pools managed per team, which is likely to shape how buyers expect to pay for agent work in sales tools too.
